newsitem.title: FRANCE: French consumers get more confident in January.
newsitem.headline: French consumers get more confident in January.

text.p: French consumer confidence picked up in January to hit its best level in more than a year, data on Tuesday showed, but economists said the improvement would not be enough to kick-start the country's sluggish economy.

Economists called the figures good news but said they showed consumers were still extremely wary because of record 12.7 percent unemployment and predicted improvement in economic activity would be slow.
"Consumer confidence is still at historically low levels," economist Serge Le Gal of Caisse des Depots said.

The institute's global confidence indicator, which samples 2,000 households, rose in January to minus 30 from minus 33 in December. The seasonally-adjusted index has been edging higher since hitting a nine-month low of minus 37 in May, 1996.

"The figures conform with our scenario that activity is picking up but not very strongly," said Le Gal, who sees economic growth of two percent this year compared with 1.3 percent last year. The government is officially targeting growth of 2.3 percent for 1997.

"We have seen a slight uptick in confidence," said economist Joanne Perez of Merrill Lynch. "We can't say it's the start of a new boom era but it looks as though we're starting to see a small bright light."

The overall index, calculated from answers to five questions covering living standards and financial and purchasing outlooks has consistently produced negative readings since it was launched in January 1987.

The best level the global confidence index ever attained was minus 11 in November 1988. Consumer confidence hit an all-time low in December 1995 of minus 38 when the country was crippled by a nationwide strike by railway workers.
Consumer expectations about future living standards posted the best rise in January, climbing to minus 34 from minus 39.
The survey also showed more people believed it was a better time to buy than the previous month with that index figure moving to minus 23 from minus 25.

But worries about unemployment, which is not included in calculating the global indicator because of the need to make the index conform with other European data, grew with the index rising to 61 from 54.
That, economists said, conformed to expectations that unemployment would climb to new peaks this year.
